findings.title: Login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid JWT was issued for the first user (admin@juice-sh.op) with an arbitrary password, which is only possible if the email SQL clause was injected (OR 1=1 short-circuits the credential check). Prior benign wrong-credential baseline returned 401 'Invalid email or password.'

findings.title: Product search SQL injection (error-based and UNION) on q parameter
findings.response_evidence: Benign q=apple: HTTP 200 {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":\"Apple Juice (1000ml)\",...},{\"id\":24,\"name\":\"Apple Pomace\",...}]} with no error. Error probe q=qwert': HTTP 500 text/html 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error'. UNION probe q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--: HTTP 200 {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":2,\"description\":3,\"price\":4,\"deluxePrice\":5,\"image\":6,\"createdAt\":7,\"updatedAt\":8,\"deletedAt\":9}]} - injected column values 2..9 are reflected back in the product fields, proving attacker-controlled UNION SELECT output.

findings.title: Unauthenticated /api/Feedbacks exposes only masked author emails (CWE-359 not confirmed)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json, unauthenticated. Body contains 8 feedback records with keys UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. No email field exists. Author emails appear only inside comment text, with the local part masked: "I love this shop! ... (***in@juice-sh.op)", "Great shop! ... (***@juice-sh.op)", "Nothing useful available here! (***der@juice-sh.op)", "... (***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Anonymous entries show "(anonymous)" with UserId null. The masked fragments do not reveal full author addresses in clear form. Recoverability of the full local part from the body alone is not demonstrated. Unauthenticated access to the records is confirmed, but the email PII disclosure criterion is not met, so CWE-359 is rejected for this endpoint. Note: the UserId values are numeric IDs, not emails.

Differential confirms boolean SQLi via out-of-band session id at high level. Security level verified as high before testing (page text 'Security level is currently: high'). findings.title: DVWA security-level form rejects requests without user_token (CSRF not confirmed)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php (session=dvwa_admin, Origin: http://attacker.example, Referer: http://attacker.example/csrf.html) form: security=low, seclev_submit=Submit, NO user_token -> HTTP 302 redirect to security.php
findings.response_evidence: The tokenless cross-origin POST returned a 302 redirect, but the follow-up GET body shows "CSRF token is incorrect" and "Security level is currently: high". The level was not changed, so the server enforces the user_token check and rejects the forged request. The session_info security_level=low field is an artifact of the request and does not reflect the server state. The page's own content reports high. The control is not missing anti-CSRF protection; the CWE-352 candidate is rejected. Limitation: the token was not tested for session binding (a token from another session). This does not change the rejection.

findings.title: Rejected: /rest/user/whoami returns no data beyond the authenticated user's entitlement
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, application/json, body {"user":{}}. The response contains an empty user object with no email, id, basket, or token fields. Session metadata reports acct2_bench@juiceshop.local with own_basket_id=7, but none of that is disclosed by the endpoint itself. Nothing beyond what the authenticated user is entitled to see is disclosed, so CWE-200 is not supported.
